subject: Legacy contract rate reconciliation — VP/CFO signoff needed
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-11 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: Legacy contract rate reconciliation — need VP/CFO signoff

Team,

Quick summary: TheraHealth (deal DH-7832) is on a legacy pilot contract with a fixed blended rate that no longer maps to their steady-state usage. They ramped 4x in May/June and their bill for June is ~3.6x the committed monthly baseline. Sales and CS flagged this to avoid churn — customer is requesting a one-time reconciliation and a short-term rate amendment while we migrate them to the standard commitment tiers.

What I'm proposing (attached: Ther a_Legacy_Usage_Report_Q2.csv + Proposed_OneOff_Rate_Amendment.pdf):
- One-time credit equal to 15% of the excess spend on the June invoice (applies only to excess over baseline)
- Temporary per-token rate reduction for the next 90 days (transition period) to a second-tier blended rate to avoid immediate spike for their customers

Rationale: preserves relationship for a high-growth customer, reduces churn risk, and gives us time to convert to a committed tier. Financial exposure estimate in attachment shows ~USD 78k impact if approved at 15%.

Ask: I need a VP/CFO signoff to proceed with the 15% one-time credit + 90-day rate amendment. Can we get clearance this week? If we need to reduce the ask to ~10% to get through faster, state it here and we can take a narrower ask to execs.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aisha@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Ther a_Legacy_Usage_Report_Q2.csv, Proposed_OneOff_Rate_Amendment.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-11 10:03 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Legacy contract rate reconciliation — need VP/CFO signoff

Aisha — thanks for the clear summary and attachments. A couple quick thoughts: 1) I agree we should prioritize retention; 2) The finance estimate looks right but I'd prefer a conservative ask to execs.

Proposal from pricing: ask for a 10% one-time credit on excess (not 15%) and the 90-day rate amendment as you described. We can include a clause that the credit is contingent on them signing a 12-month commitment at the new committed tier by the end of the 90 days. This reduces our downside and gives commercial leverage.

Marcus — can you run a quick sensitivity (10% vs 15%) and confirm P&L impact to rev recognition? Marissa — can you prep a short executive memo we can pass to the VP/CFO? I can take the first pass on the finance blurb.

-Karthik

--

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@therahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-11 11:25 AM PDT
Subject: Re: TheraHealth usage spike — proposed reconciliation and short-term rate amendment

Daniel,

Thanks again for walking through the usage run-rate with us this morning. Attached is our proposed reconciliation and a temporary rate amendment to smooth the ramp while you finalize your long-term forecast. High level:
- One-time credit to offset 10% of the excess usage over your baseline for June (we're proposing 10% with exec approval in flight)
- Temporary blended rate for the next 90 days (matches the second-tier commitment)
- Contingent commitment: if you convert to a 12-month committed tier within the 90-day window, we will (retroactively) apply the full reconciliation credit up to 15% as discussed on the call.

We're trying to be pragmatic — we want TheraHealth to succeed and we also need to control near-term finance exposure. If that sounds reasonable I'll route the papers for the signoff and DocuSign.

Best,
Aisha
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Proposed_OneOff_Rate_Amendment.pdf
From: Daniel Park <daniel@therahealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12 08:42 AM PDT
Subject: Re: TheraHealth usage spike — proposed reconciliation and short-term rate amendment

Aisha / team,

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the constructive approach. The proposal is reasonable. Two quick asks before we sign: 1) can the temporary rate amendment include a 30-day exit notice in case usage patterns revert? 2) if we convert to the 12-month commitment within 90 days, please make the retroactive credit automatic rather than subject to additional negotiation.

If you can confirm those two points I'll route internally and expect to return a signed DocuSign within 72 hours.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Engineering Ops, TheraHealth Inc.
daniel@therahealth.com
